content: The provided text is a detailed and technical summary of evidence-based recommendations and quality assessments for the prevention and treatment of maternal peripartum infections, as outlined by the World Health Organization (WHO). 1. Maternal Urinary Tract Infections: A single randomized trial assessed the use of antibiotics for preventing maternal urinary tract infections. The study showed no significant events (0/27 and 0/32 cases in the respective groups). The evidence quality was rated as very low due to serious limitations in study design and imprecision. 2. Maternal Composite Serious Infectious Complications: One randomized trial evaluated the prevention of serious infectious complications in mothers. No events were reported (0/27 and 0/32 cases in the respective groups). The evidence was not pooled, and the quality was rated as very low due to serious design limitations and imprecision. 3. Maternal Composite Adverse Effects: Two randomized trials investigated adverse effects in mothers. No events were observed (0/172 and 0/187 cases in the respective groups). The evidence was not pooled, and the quality was rated as very low due to serious design limitations and imprecision. 4. Maternal Allergic Reactions: A single randomized trial assessed allergic reactions in mothers. No events were reported (0/27 and 0/32 cases in the respective groups). The evidence was not pooled, and the quality was rated as very low due to serious design limitations and imprecision. 5. Maternal Nausea: One randomized trial evaluated maternal nausea. No events were observed (0/27 and 0/32 cases in the respective groups). The evidence was not pooled, and the quality was rated as very low due to serious design limitations and imprecision. 6. Maternal Vomiting: A single randomized trial assessed maternal vomiting. No events were reported (0/27 and 0/32 cases in the respective groups). The evidence was not pooled, and the quality was rated as very low due to serious design limitations and imprecision. 7. Maternal Diarrhea: One randomized trial evaluated maternal diarrhea. No events were observed (0/27 and 0/32 cases in the respective groups). The evidence was not pooled, and the quality was rated as very low due to serious design limitations and imprecision. 8. Maternal Skin Rash: A single randomized trial assessed maternal skin rash. No events were reported (0/27 and 0/32 cases in the respective groups). The evidence was not pooled, and the quality was rated as very low due to serious design limitations and imprecision. 9. Prophylactic Antibiotics for Cesarean Section: Various classes of antibiotics, including third-generation cephalosporins, penicillins, fluoroquinolones, and macrolides, were compared for their effectiveness in preventing infections during cesarean sections. The evidence quality was consistently rated as very low due to serious design limitations, wide confidence intervals crossing the line of no effect, small sample sizes, and few events. 10. Antibiotic Regimens for Intra-amniotic Infections (Chorioamnionitis): Antibiotic regimens for managing intra-amniotic infections during labor and postpartum were evaluated. The evidence quality was rated as very low due to serious design limitations, imprecision, and small sample sizes. 11. Antibiotic Regimens for Postpartum Endometritis: Various antibiotic regimens, including combinations of lincosamides, aminoglycosides, penicillins, and beta-lactamase inhibitors, were assessed for treating postpartum endometritis. The evidence quality was rated as very low due to serious design limitations, imprecision, and small sample sizes. 12. Adverse Effects of Antibiotic Regimens: Adverse effects such as diarrhea and other complications were evaluated for different antibiotic regimens. The evidence quality was consistently rated as very low due to serious design limitations, imprecision, and small sample sizes.
